_doc: Modern Japanese general hospital. No floor plan is provided: every room is hideOnMap with no offsetX/offsetY, so the building only exists as the room list + the connects graph below. Room-to-room travel is abstracted as a hub-and-spoke layout with approximate walking minutes as door cost (Door_Instance cost = ticks spent on that hop, see ActionPackage_PathTo). Abstract layout: 1F outpatient lobby (reception + waiting, also the world-map exit) with triage and the pharmacy counter just off it; the inpatient ward is upstairs, reached by elevator into the ward corridor that the patient rooms open onto. Patient rooms are numbered 301/302/303/305 - Japanese hospitals conventionally skip 4 (shi = death).
_doc_sandboxing: Staff sandbox by workModule.workCommands: each finished command picks a new random one, and each command is only offered by furniture in one room type, so staff drift between rooms (convenience store / high school pattern). Every hospital command carries a role tag (jp_hospital_doctor / _nurse / _pharmacy / _frontdesk / _visitor / _patient) for tag-matching behavior nodes. Pharmacy and front desk staff have a single workCommand each, so they stay in their room all shift; nurses do not sandbox by workCommands at all - their behavior_job override (TryFindNurseJobNode) picks hospital-wide cleaning first, then any jp_hospital_nurse command outside empty patient rooms. Patient/visitor commands are non-job (no 'job' tag) so their behavior_job override (TryFindNonJobByTagNode) can find them by tag. Hospital commands deliberately avoid the generic 'bed'/'rest'/'recreation' tags so they are never picked up by other furniture's comTags givers or the generic rest/recreation searches.
_doc_pay: Hourly pay approximates 2025 MHLW wage census averages (nurse ~5.25M JPY/yr over ~1920h, salaried doctor ~15.12M JPY/yr over ~2520h), plus the 25% legal late-night premium for 22:00-05:00, 35% holiday premium for weekend doctors (doctors work a 14-day 12h rota, so both premiums are averaged into each team's flat rate - see the doctor MemberType's _comment_rota), and the JNA 2024 overnight night allowance (5715 JPY per shift) spread over the nurses' 12h night shift (nurses work the same rota - see the nurse MemberType's _comment_rota).

factionInit._comment_isRentingFloor: hospital owns its own building outright
factionInit._comment_meals: Non-player faction: mealHours stay fixed (only player factions clear them daily and rebuild them via com_furniture_mealPrep, see Manageable.OnDayUpdate_0 / ActionPackage beginMealPrep). Taking an item from a non-player faction's inventory hands out a fresh copy without depleting stock (Inventory.RemoveItem), so a single meal item is enough. Meals are served by furniture_marker_getmeal in the patient rooms.
factionInit._comment_salesInventory: sold over the pharmacy counter (furniture_marker_jp_hospital_pharmacy_counter in hospital_pharmacy)
factionInit._comment_assignableMemberTypes: Parent IDs stand for every shift under them (Manageable.AssignableMemberTypes).
factionInit._comment_joinableMemberTypes: MemberTypes this faction can be joined as through the reachable-faction searches (FactionJoinUtility: Labor_Start admission, the join-by-tag dialogue options). Their joinHandler still decides who is admitted.
factionInit._comment_fallbackWorkers: Per-shift staffing: headcount = total wanted on shift, maxFallback = most fallback workers used. templateIDs = CharaTemplateGenerators from JP_World/Characters/templates.json. Each fallback worker is generated for exactly one of these memberTypeIDs and stays pinned to it (Manageable_WorkerPool.assignedMemberTypes). Pharmacy/front desk reuse the nurse template until dedicated clerk portrait bases exist.
factionInit._comment_hourlyEvents: Started every hour on the hospital's own patients (Manageable.StartHourlyEvents) - staff dispatch, see Events/hospital_medical_dispatch.json.

floorPlans._comment_imagePath: PLACEHOLDER - Floor_Base.OnAfterDeserialize marks a floor invalid when imagePath is empty, so this must stay non-empty. Point it at the hospital exterior image once it exists. No room is drawn on it (all hideOnMap). All room images below are also placeholders borrowed from BA_Utnapishtim/Media_UI_Scenario_Background, to be replaced with generated assets.
floorPlans._comment_isFloorPlan: false = imagePath is a straight background image (canvas_RoomDisplay.bgpicture), not a floor plan, so no room coordinates are needed.
floorPlans._comment_wholeBuildingRent: hospital owns the building (isRentingFloor:false), so only maintenanceFee applies; NPC faction, never actually charged in practice
floorPlans._comment_travel: Approximate walking minutes per hop. lobby->triage 1, lobby->pharmacy 1, lobby->ward corridor 3 (walk to elevator + ride + walk out), triage->ward corridor 3 (staff/bed elevator used when admitting), corridor->301/302 1, corridor->303/305 2 (further down the corridor), neighbouring patient rooms 1. Worst case entrance->305 = 5 min, well under the 99 total-path-cost cap.
floorPlans._comment_patientRooms: furniture_bed_hospital's ID contains 'furniture_bed', which makes each patient room private (Room_Instance.isRoomPrivate). Staff commands offered there set allowInPrivateRoom so staff still reach them.

rooms._comment_roomImagePath: PLACEHOLDER - reuses the lobby image until a corridor image exists

memberTypes._comment: Parent of the doctor shifts (MemberType hierarchy): never held - joining as it joins the first child. The shifts are defined inline (childMemberTypes, first = default) and registered as ordinary MemberTypes; each inherits every field it leaves out and only states its own workModule.
memberTypes._comment_behaviorOverrides: behavior_job override to be authored later; until then the default TryFindScheduledJobNode dispatches workCommands.
memberTypes._comment_rota: 12-hour Pitman rota over a 14-day cycle (activeDays: 0-6 = week A Mon-Sun, 7-13 = week B; week A = the week of the campaign start). Week A: team A days and team B nights on Mon Tue Fri Sat Sun, team C days and team D nights on Wed Thu; week B swaps A/B with C/D. Every day has exactly one day team (07:00-19:00) and one night team (19:00-07:00) on; each team works 7 shifts per 14 days including 2 weekend days. A night shift's morning hours count for the day it started (WorkModuleInit.IsActiveAt). Pay: day 6000 base, night 6875 = 12h average of base with the 25% late-night premium for 22:00-05:00; both +10% = the 35% holiday premium averaged over 2 weekend shifts in 7.

memberTypes._comment: Parent of the nurse shifts (MemberType hierarchy): never held - joining as it joins the first child. The shifts are defined inline (childMemberTypes, first = default) and registered as ordinary MemberTypes; each inherits every field it leaves out and only states its own workModule.
memberTypes._comment_behaviorOverrides: TryFindNurseJobNode replaces the schedule's random workCommand: first any cleaning job anywhere in the hospital, then any job-tagged jp_hospital_nurse command, skipping private rooms with no assigned owner (empty patient rooms). workCommands stay listed for documentation / the shift schedule only.
memberTypes._comment_rota: Same 12-hour Pitman rota as the doctors (see membertype_jp_hospital_doctor _comment_rota): 14-day cycle, team A days / team B nights on week A Mon Tue Fri Sat Sun + week B Wed Thu, teams C/D the other days. Exactly one day team (07:00-19:00) and one night team (19:00-07:00) on every day. Pay: day 2500 base (no weekend premium for nurses, as before); night 3340 = 12h average of base with the 25% late-night premium for 22:00-05:00 (2865) + the JNA overnight allowance 5715 per shift spread over 12h (476).

memberTypes._comment: Assigned as a TEMP home faction on admission. initiallyForbidWork keeps the patient from leaving for their work factions while the hospital is their priority home. No workModule: the hospital is their active faction by being their priority home.
memberTypes._comment_cannotRequestLeaveMemberTypes: A patient never asks doctors or nurses to leave, whatever the reason (RequestLeaveUtility.CanRequestLeave). Parent IDs cover every shift.
memberTypes._comment_joinHandler: Builds the admission options (JoinActiveFaction Result in jp_hospital_Opt_Admit) - logic lives in JoinHandler_HospitalPatient.
memberTypes._comment_leaveHandler: Builds the discharge options (LeaveActiveFaction Result in jp_hospital_Opt_Discharge) - logic lives in LeaveHandler_HospitalPatient.

memberTypes._comment: Assigned as a WORK faction. The command-less workModule makes the hospital the visitor's active faction during visiting hours (brings them here via TryChangeLocaleNode). behavior_job looks for commands tagged jp_hospital_visitor; none exist yet (the generic wait commands in COM_Defs/com_furniture_wait.json don't carry it), so visitors fall through to sandbox behavior.
memberTypes._comment_joinHandler: Builds one visit option per patient (JoinActiveFaction Result in jp_hospital_Opt_Visit) - logic lives in JoinHandler_HospitalVisitor.
memberTypes._comment_leaveHandler: Builds the end-visit options (LeaveActiveFaction Result in jp_hospital_Opt_EndVisit) - logic lives in LeaveHandler_HospitalVisitor.

list._comment: The sole provider of 'wait'-tagged commands. furnitureSize 0 = no actor cap (Job_Furniture.CanCOMAcceptMoreActor / ActionPackage_Interaction.AllowJoining).

ID must contain 'furniture_bed' so the room counts as private. Offers the generic sleep command, the patient-only bed rest, and the generic com_furniture_rest_required (labor / recovery) - deliberately NOT the generic comTags [furniture, bed] set.

list._comment: One command = 2 hours of bed rest, modeled on com_furniture_takingLongBreak. req_Doers.requireJobFaction Home limits it to characters whose priority home is the hospital (patients). No generic 'bed'/'rest' tags on purpose. 'rest_required' marks it as bed rest for labor (ReproductionUtility.CanBirthNow) - without it a patient resting here never entered active labor.

Hospital meal tray. Deliberately no ItemComponent_Degradable (so it never spoils out of the hospital's one-item stock) and no 'industrial' tag (so shops matching industrial consumables don't sell it).
